shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures recouped early losses to close little changed on Thursday, as support from rising crude oil prices and a firmer Shanghai market countered pressure from weaker Tokyo equities.($1 = 158.1700 yen)($1 = 6.7019 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures recouped early losses to close little changed on Thursday, as support from rising crude oil prices and a firmer Shanghai market countered pressure from weaker Tokyo equities.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for March delivery
was little changed at 457.7 yen ($2.89) per kg
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 435 yuan, or 2.21%, to 20,145 yuan ($3,005.86) per metric ton
It surged to its highest level since February 21, 2017, earlier in the day, as the market reopened after China's week-long National Day holiday
The most-active November butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) surged 720 yuan, or 4.54%, to 16,590 yuan per ton
Japanese shares fell more than 1% in their second straight session of losses, as investors paused after recent rallies, wary of the US rate outlook, higher yields and geopolitical tensions
Weaker risk sentiment tends to weigh on rubber futures

Oil prices rose on persistent worries about supply from the key Middle East producing region amid an increase in attacks on shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, while the US cut output as a hurricane menaced offshore production
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil
Indonesia's natural rubber exports totalled 864,000 tons in the first eight months of 2026, down 21% year-on-year, data from rubber information provider Qinrex showed
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for January delivery (STFF7) was last flat at 256.1 U.S. cents per kg, as of 0700 GMT
